title: Search click aggregator restarted by scheduler

brief.headline: Continuity Guardian escalated
brief.what_broke: 12 session(s) waiting on locks. Root blocker(s): pid 1456575 (batch_worker/batch_replayable_search_click_aggregate, idle in transaction, txn open 4.2s) blocks 1 session(s); last statement: SELECT 1
brief.who_is_affected: Checkout success 77% over 10s (7/30 failed) vs SLO 95%. Revenue run-rate $18,400/min; about $4,293/min at risk. Verification window 10s. The business tolerates at most 60s of degraded checkout.

options.description: Terminate the root blocker session (batch_worker/batch_replayable_search_click_aggregate, pid 1456575) to release its locks.
Take no action; let the blocker finish and monitor checkout recovery.
options.cost: about $4,293/min of checkout revenue at risk while waiting

brief.recommendation: Revenue at risk $4,293/min; SLO 95% success over 10s verification; blocker runtime 4.2s fits within tolerated 60s degradation; escalation needed because critical probes (workload registry, change calendar, protected settlements, tradeoff) are missing, preventing automated termination decision.

audit.report: The search click aggregator restart triggered a checkout degradation (77% success vs 95% SLO, $4,293/min revenue at risk). A batch worker (batch_replayable_search_click_aggregate, pid 1456575) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4.2s with last statement SELECT 1, blocking checkout sessions. Both guardians agreed to escalate because critical probes (workload registry, change calendar, protected settlements) were missing and memory only verified termination safety for other batch_replayable jobs, not this specific workload. The incident was escalated to on-call after 99.4s; no automated action was taken.
audit.root_cause: batch_replayable_search_click_aggregate (pid 1456575) held an idle-in-transaction lock for 4.2s (last statement SELECT 1), blocking checkout sessions and degrading success to 77% vs 95% SLO.
lessons: Register batch_replayable_search_click_aggregate in biz.workload_registry with verified termination safety evidence; current memory (MEM-1) only covers batch_replayable_subscription_renewal_retry and batch_replayable_returns_label_prefetch.
Investigate why batch_replayable_search_click_aggregate enters idle-in-transaction state with SELECT 1; this application-level pattern caused the blocking.
audit.negotiation_critique: Both guardians correctly identified missing evidence and reached consensus to escalate in a single round (99.4s) with no wasted rounds; Database Guardian cited the specific memory gap (MEM-1 covers other batch_replayable jobs only), and Continuity Guardian confirmed the 4.2s blocker fits within the 60s tolerance but missing probes prevent automation.
follow_ups: Add batch_replayable_search_click_aggregate to the workload registry with a termination safety classification.
Implement the missing critical probes: biz.workload_registry, biz.change_calendar, and db.protected_settlement.
Root-cause the idle-in-transaction SELECT 1 pattern in the search click aggregator batch worker code.

proposal.rationale: The blocking workload (pid 1456575, batch_worker/batch_replayable_search_click_aggregate) lacks verified evidence that terminating it will restore checkout; memory recalls success only for other batch_replayable jobs (batch_replayable_subscription_renewal_retry, batch_replayable_returns_label_prefetch). Critical probes are missing (biz.workload_registry, biz.change_calendar, db.protected_settlements, biz.tradeoff), making the trade‑off unsuitable for an automated decision. Escalation hands the decision to the owning team with a decision brief that includes the available evidence and the need for further data.
proposal.expected_effect: The owning team will review the incident, request any additional probes they deem necessary, and decide whether to terminate the blocker, wait, or take other action. This avoids an ill‑informed termination that could disrupt other processes.
proposal.risk_assessment: Delaying action may allow the blocker to persist beyond the 60‑second tolerance window, increasing checkout timeout rate (currently 55% success, 27 timeouts in 15s) and revenue at risk (~$4,293/min). However, proceeding with termination without evidence could inadvertently kill a critical batch job and cause broader service degradation.
